predictions.text: The title 'data scientist' will be gone by 2032. It will all be analytics engineer.
We ran an A/B test with 38,000 users per arm over 21 days. Lift in conversion was 1.8% with a p-value of 0.008. Power analysis at 80% needed roughly 9k per arm, so we were adequately powered.

Embedding comparison on 30,000 labeled support tickets: TF-IDF + logistic regression hit 0.76 macro-F1 while a fine-tuned BERT-base got 0.88. GPU inference cost $1.10 per 1k tickets versus effectively zero for TF-IDF.
Cleaning notes: 2.8% of rows had null income. Median imputation vs a iterative imputer changed downstream AUC by 0.003 over 5-fold CV, which is within the fold-to-fold std of 0.006.

Class imbalance was 1:45 in our fraud set. SMOTE gave PR-AUC 0.28, while simply using class weights and tuning the threshold got 0.39. Calibration (Brier score 0.021) was also better without resampling.

Our dbt job was timing out. Repartitioning from 64 to 128 partitions and broadcasting the 300MB lookup table dropped wall-clock from 52 min to 9 min. Shuffle spill went to near zero according to the Spark UI.
Just defended my masters thesis! Data science here I come. So grateful and a little terrified.
Prediction: time series forecasting will be the next big skill, and everyone who ignores it is going to get left behind.

Switching our pandas groupby-apply to a vectorized merge + cumsum version cut the feature pipeline from 2.5 hours to 3 minutes on 40M rows. Profiling with cProfile showed the apply lambda was 91% of runtime.
